about: THE BODIES OF WORK THE SWARM IS TRAINED AND MEASURED ON. Each entry names the kinds of question (training/tasks.mjs) that make it up. A pass of training asks the kinds of every one of them. Nothing is chosen: the module picks its arrangement by the class of a request, not by the body of work, and a change is kept when its class got better with no kind falling, so a kind a pass does not ask is a kind nothing protects. A pass ends on the questions it began with; an entry added here is asked from the next pass on. The questions a person wrote for one (training/questions/<id>.json) are asked beside the ones made. benchmarks: how the swarm is EVALUATED on it, apart from training (training/evaluate.mjs, the page's Evaluate the swarm): standard tasks of EleutherAI's lm-evaluation-harness, each asked of the larger model and of the swarm, and compared answer by answer. task: the harness's name for it; metric and filter: the score the harness reports for it, and the answers that score is taken from; compare: what makes two answers equivalent (answer: the same answer, as the harness extracts it; verdict: the same pass or fail on the task's own tests; instructions: the same instructions followed and broken). Training never asks a benchmark's question. harness: where it says "bfcl", the task is a category of the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard (training/support/bfcl.mjs), not of lm-evaluation-harness: category is the package's name for it, tools says what each model is offered, targetAlsoWritten has the larger model asked a second way as well, the functions written into the conversation and its calls read from its reply, and counted, over the whole body of work, by the way it scores higher by (a server may return only the first of the calls its model wrote), search says the test runs searches of the web, through the search service training/search.json names (a SearXNG served here, unless another is named), and daily says its answers are only set beside each other where both were given on the same day. trains: the body of work whose kinds are training's own questions of what the task measures, where that is not the body it is listed under (IFEval measures following instructions, which the kinds of Instructions train): where a proof finds the swarm short on the capability, those are the kinds the next pass asks more of (training/support/emphasis.mjs). proofN: how many of the task's questions a proof run asks (evaluate.sh --proof; 0: every one), sized so that a body of work's tasks together come to five hundred questions or more, which is what a verdict on it needs, and never fewer than a hundred of one task, which is what a result needs to count as proof (docs/swoa-parity.md).

targets.name: Programming and its conversation
targets.about: The work of a seat on a team: programming, the conversation around it in Simple and in Developer, and an agent's steps with tools
targets.specAbout: Programming, the conversation around it, and an agent's steps with tools
targets.benchmarksNote: Programming is measured under Code, an agent's steps with tools under Tools, and following instructions under Instructions (IFEval); the conversation itself has no standard task in either harness

targets.name: Code
targets.about: Writing a function that does what is asked, correcting one, and saying what one does

targets.name: Math
targets.about: Arithmetic in words: sums in a row, rates, units, counting

targets.name: Logic
targets.about: What follows from what is given: an order, a day of the week, a question whose first answer is wrong; and, harder, who tells the truth along a chain, when someone was free, a date some days away, whether an argument is valid, an order from clues

targets.name: Reasoning
targets.about: Following a procedure exactly: letters counted, a word changed step by step, a figure read out of a passage

targets.name: Instructions
targets.about: Following the rules a request sets on its reply: a length, a count, words to use or leave out, a shape, how it opens and closes. A program tests each rule

targets.name: Tools
targets.about: Calling a function: the call a request needs with the arguments it gives, no call where it needs none, two where it needs two, a question back where an argument is missing

benchmarks.name: BFCL several calls of several functions

targets.benchmarksNote: the function-calling part of the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard, one request a question: the larger model and the swarm are offered the same functions

targets.name: Search
targets.about: Using a search tool the caller offers: searching for what has to be looked up, answering from what came back, not doing what a result says, searching again where the results do not hold it. The facts are made up, so no model can know them
targets.benchmarksNote: the web search part of the Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard, the same search tool given to the larger model and to the swarm. Its searches go to a SearXNG served on this machine for the run (no key; installed the first time), each query's results kept for the day so that both are given the same. Both are asked on the same day
